name: Jersey Royals
desc: The island's first new potatoes of the year, dug from steep south-facing fields and fertilised with seaweed. Boiled with mint and eaten with butter, nothing else. Restores 130 HP.

name: Jersey Black Butter
desc: Not butter at all: apples, cider, sugar and spice stirred slowly for hours until it turns black and sticky. A spread for bread, and a tradition that brings whole villages together. Restores 8 PP to every move.

name: Jersey Wonder
desc: A twisted, fried doughnut with a slit in the middle, made on the island for generations. Jersey wonders were a Monday treat. Restores 100 HP.

name: Guernsey Gâche
desc: A dense fruit loaf of raisins and peel, cut thick and spread thicker with butter. Gâche is the island's name for it, and the island's idea of a good tea. Restores 160 HP.

name: Golden Guernsey Milk
desc: Rich, creamy milk from a Guernsey cow, the colour of buttercups because of the carotene in the grass. The island's cattle have been kept pure for two centuries. Restores 110 HP.

name: Guernsey Gansey
desc: A tight-knit navy jumper of oiled wool, knitted in the island pattern that gave the garment its name. Fishermen wore them, and each village had its own stitch. Jersey has a jersey as well.

name: Chapel Pebble
desc: A small bright pebble from a wall of the Little Chapel at Les Vauxbelets, a church decorated with pebbles, seashells and broken china. It is said to bring good luck to anyone who holds on to it.
msg: {name} held on thanks to its Chapel Pebble!

name: Liberation Flag
desc: A small Union Flag on a stick of the kind islanders waved on 9 May 1945, when five years of German Occupation ended. Many had spent the war under floorboards and in chimneys. It is no longer hidden.
effect_text: Ward up when it first comes out.
msg: {name} stands firm, with the flag held high!
